commands.cmd:
V=$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Version}' systemd) || { echo "SYSTEMD_PIN_FAIL: dpkg-query failed"; exit 1; }
ST=$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' systemd)
C=$(systemctl --version | head -1)
OWN=$(dpkg -S /usr/bin/systemctl /usr/bin/systemd-run | cut -d: -f1 | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
ORIGIN=$(apt-cache policy systemd 2>/dev/null | awk '/^ \*\*\* /{f=1; print; next} f && /^ +[0-9]+ http/{print; next} f{exit}' | sed 's/^ *//' | tr '\n' ';')
python3 - "$V" "$ST" "$C" "$OWN" "$ORIGIN" <<'PY'
import glob, json, sys
v, status, ctl, owners, origin = sys.argv[1:6]
stack = sorted({x['version'] for x in json.load(open('manifests/stack.json'))['components'] if x['id'] == 'systemd'})
winners = sorted({w['pin'] for f in glob.glob('catalogs/landscape/*.json') for l in json.load(open(f)).get('layers', []) for w in (l.get('winners') or []) if w.get('component_id') == 'systemd'})
ok = stack == winners == [v] and v in ctl and status == 'install ok installed' and owners.split() == ['systemd'] and origin.startswith('*** ' + v) and 'noble-updates' in origin and 'noble-security' in origin
print('SYSTEMD_PIN_' + ('OK' if ok else 'FAIL'), '| dpkg-query systemd', v, '(' + status + ') | systemctl --version:', ctl, '| stack', stack, 'winner', winners)
print('install source: Ubuntu package; /usr/bin/systemctl and /usr/bin/systemd-run owned by package:', owners.strip(), '| apt-cache policy:', origin)
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
PY

commands.cmd:
UNIT="nas-receipt-probe-$$-$(date +%s%N)"
OUT=$(timeout 60 systemd-run --user --wait --pipe --collect --unit="$UNIT" -p Type=exec -p RuntimeMaxSec=30s -p TimeoutStopSec=5s -p KillMode=control-group -p SendSIGKILL=yes -p MemoryAccounting=yes -p MemoryMax=256M -p CPUAccounting=yes -p TasksAccounting=yes -p TasksMax=32 -p NoNewPrivileges=yes --working-directory="$(pwd)" /usr/bin/python3 scripts/validate_catalogs.py 2>&1)
RC=$?
FIN=$(printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep '^Finished with result: ')
MAIN=$(printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep '^Main processes terminated with: ')
VAL=$(printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -c '^Catalog structure and evidence classes validated')
n=0
LEFT=$(systemctl --user show "$UNIT.service" --property=LoadState --value)
while [ "$LEFT" != "not-found" ] && [ "$n" -lt 20 ]; do sleep 0.1; n=$((n + 1)); LEFT=$(systemctl --user show "$UNIT.service" --property=LoadState --value); done
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ "$FIN" = "Finished with result: success" ] && [ "$MAIN" = "Main processes terminated with: code=exited/status=0" ] && [ "$VAL" -eq 1 ] && [ "$LEFT" = "not-found" ]; then
  echo "SYSTEMD_WORKLOAD_OK | systemd-run --user --wait exit $RC | $FIN | $MAIN | validator line present: $VAL | unit after --collect: $LEFT"
else
  echo "SYSTEMD_WORKLOAD_FAIL | systemd-run exit $RC | $FIN | $MAIN | validator line present: $VAL | unit after --collect: $LEFT"
  printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | tail -20
  exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -E '^(Running as unit|Service runtime|CPU time consumed|Memory peak)'

commands.cmd:
UNIT="nas-receipt-timer-$$-$(date +%s%N)"
MARK="nas_timer_probe_$$_ok"
timeout 20 systemd-run --user --unit="$UNIT" --on-active=2s --timer-property=AccuracySec=100ms -p Type=exec -p RemainAfterExit=yes -p RuntimeMaxSec=10s -p SyslogIdentifier="$UNIT" --working-directory="$(pwd)" /bin/sh -c "test -f manifests/stack.json && test -f catalogs/landscape/foundation.json && echo $MARK" > /dev/null 2>&1
RC0=$?
i=0
SHOW=""
while [ "$i" -lt 15 ]; do
  SHOW=$(systemctl --user show "$UNIT.service" --property=LoadState,Result,ExecMainCode,ExecMainStatus,ActiveState,SubState)
  case "$SHOW" in *ActiveState=active*) case "$SHOW" in *SubState=exited*) break ;; esac ;; esac
  i=$((i + 1))
  sleep 1
done
j=0
MARKED=0
while [ "$j" -lt 10 ]; do
  if journalctl --user -t "$UNIT" --no-pager -o cat 2> /dev/null | grep -qx "$MARK"; then MARKED=1; break; fi
  j=$((j + 1))
  sleep 1
done
systemctl --user stop "$UNIT.timer" "$UNIT.service" > /dev/null 2>&1
systemctl --user reset-failed "$UNIT.service" "$UNIT.timer" > /dev/null 2>&1
GONE=$(systemctl --user show "$UNIT.service" --property=LoadState --value)
if [ "$RC0" -eq 0 ] && [ "$MARKED" -eq 1 ] && printf '%s\n' "$SHOW" | grep -qx 'LoadState=loaded' && printf '%s\n' "$SHOW" | grep -qx 'Result=success' && printf '%s\n' "$SHOW" | grep -qx 'ExecMainCode=1' && printf '%s\n' "$SHOW" | grep -qx 'ExecMainStatus=0' && [ "$GONE" = "not-found" ]; then
  echo "SYSTEMD_TIMER_OK | timer fired its service (poll $i s): $(printf '%s' "$SHOW" | tr '\n' ' ')| journal marker line under SyslogIdentifier=$UNIT: $MARK | after stop: LoadState=$GONE"
else
  echo "SYSTEMD_TIMER_FAIL | schedule exit $RC0 | marker seen: $MARKED | $(printf '%s' "$SHOW" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  exit 1
fi

claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925 (WSL2 x86_64), systemd 255.4-1ubuntu8.17, the scheduling-supervision winner, supervises real bounded work as the user manager. dpkg-query reports the installed Ubuntu package systemd 255.4-1ubuntu8.17, systemctl --version agrees, the stack and winner pins read the same version, and apt-cache policy lists it from noble-updates and noble-security. A transient user service (systemd-run --user --wait --pipe --collect with memory, task and runtime limits) runs the repository's catalog validator; systemd-run exits 0, systemd reports 'Finished with result: success' and 'Main processes terminated with: code=exited/status=0', and the validator's success line is present. A unit that exits 7 is reported as Result=exit-code, ExecMainStatus=7, ActiveState=failed, and a unit that exceeds RuntimeMaxSec is reported as Result=timeout, ActiveState=failed (positive controls). A transient timer fires its service, which systemd reports as Result=success with ExecMainStatus=0, and its marker line reaches the journal under the service's own SyslogIdentifier. Every unit is gone afterwards. Every command exits 0 on its own assertions.
limitations: Supersedes nativestack-5975wx-20260925--systemd--use--20260926 (generation 1 of this date), which is kept and failed: its timer command found no marker line with journalctl --user -u <unit>, although systemd reported the timer's service as Result=success, ExecMainStatus=0. The journal holds that line, but journald stored it without _SYSTEMD_USER_UNIT or _SYSTEMD_CGROUP (only SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER=sh), because the service's shell had exited before journald attributed it, and the -u filter depends on that attribution; the passing dry runs had it. This generation gives the timer's service a unique SyslogIdentifier, which systemd attaches to its output stream, and reads the marker with journalctl --user -t; the other four commands are unchanged. Generation 1 is a native_proven fail, so while it was the latest systemd use receipt for this host it blocked accepted in scripts/platform_status.py; a later pass for the same host and stage clears that.

Also replaces nativestack-5975wx-20260925--systemd--use--20260925-2 as this host's latest systemd use receipt. It is a new dated receipt, not a further generation: record --supersedes links generations only within one date, and the 2026-09-25 receipts stay unchanged. They still count in scripts/platform_status.py, which counts every independently agreed native_proven pass, unless a reviewer records needs_changes on them. The cross-family review of #281 found that its retained excerpt stopped before the claimed successful result and status lines; this receipt prints them first, reads the timer service's result from systemd instead of inferring it from the marker, and checks LoadState=loaded before relying on any unit property.
Transient units only: no persistent unit, enablement, linger, reboot or power-loss behaviour is exercised; those remain the layer's open recovery gaps.
WSL2's systemd runs inside the WSL VM; host (Windows) restarts are out of scope.
